citations.assessment: The list of Temple officials expressly assigns Elazar to the curtains.
The retrieved Tosafot cites Abba bar Zimna in Rabbi Eliezer Ze’ira’s name. The gloss reports Elazar Ze’ira and proposes deleting the first name. Preserve the difference.
Ivo’s account of the willow uses Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok in the retrieved Bavli. The related episode repeats that form.
The internal heading supplies the gloss’s intended dossier. The pointer leaves the reported alternatives distinct.
The digital edition supplies bracketed Tzadok in both occurrences. The gloss reports Yitzchak at the first and Tzadok when the same subject returns.
The ordination list in the digital source reads Elazar ben Shammua, agreeing with the gloss’s proposed reading.
The present text has Rabban Gamliel the Elder and a parenthetic expansion to ben Azaryah. The gloss conjectures ben Arakh on chronological grounds.
The digital mishnah has Elazar and the discussion at 26a has Eliezer. Preserve the gloss’s proposed correction as a proposal.
The retrieved Mishnah and Gemara read Eliezer. The consulted Rashi and Tosafot likewise give Eliezer at the quoted loci, while the gloss proposes Elazar ben Shammua.
The digital Eruvin still says Eliezer asked Rav. The gloss suggests Elazar.
The digital Hachovel has Elazar asking Rav and retains Elazar in the continuation.
The Mishnah has the Tzadok clause, followed by distinct baraita statements from Pelimo and Elazar son of Shimon. This agrees with the gloss’s proposed resolution.
Rashi names Rabbi Elazar son of Shimon and points forward to the second chapter’s different sanctification rule.
The objection names Rabbi Elazar. The reply about setting one person against another is accompanied by an alternative distinguishing asking from mentioning.
The digital folio gives the ruling through Rav Chisda, the distinct attribution compared in the gloss.
The digital parallel explicitly gives Rabbi Elazar. Retain Rav Chisda’s separate attribution on 6a.

The exact Yuchasin entry and the best witness for the Ze’ira formula remain open. The cited Tosafot names the transmitter. Its digital text differs from both the gloss’s report and its proposed deletion.
Yuchasin’s reported Yitzchak patronym requires a direct witness. Compared the Bavli stories, which use Tzadok. The gloss’s variant and reservation remain visible.

The chronological objection and abbreviation’s alternate expansion remain conjectures. The Semachot witness supplies ben Azaryah parenthetically; the consulted wording does not establish the ben Arakh proposal.

The proposed identity and three-place correction need printed collation and the author’s fuller proof. Compared the full local Mishnah/Gemara transmission and cited commentators. Retained the gloss in its own voice.

The exact Tosafot analogy for the teacherhood inference remains open. The available Yoma 4a and 4b commentary did not establish the specific clause. Preserve attributed reasoning without generalizing it to the curtain official.
